paras: The Beal Street automobile shooting was an attack in Memphis, Tennessee, in March 1919, in which two white men firing from an automobile killed James Anderson, a Black man, and wounded three other Black men as they came out of a cafe on Beal street. The men escaped, and police had not identified them when the only known report was published.

According to a Memphis dispatch printed on March 22, 1919, the shooting took place "early today"; the dispatch itself carries no date. Earlier that night, a group of Black men riding in a large automobile met another car carrying "several white men" on Fourth street and were fired upon, "but without effect." Later, on Beal street, two white men seated in an automobile opened fire on Black men as they emerged from a cafe, killing Anderson and wounding three others, whose names were not given. The dispatch said it was "supposed" that the same white men had done the shooting in both encounters.
The two gunmen escaped in a small automobile, and police that night were "still hunting for clews" to their identity. No report of an arrest, inquest or trial was found in the coverage.

The shooting is known from a single brief in the Ohio State Monitor, a Black weekly, which printed it on its front page on March 22, 1919, under the headline "MEMPHIS NEGRO KILLED" and the subhead "Fired Upon by Two White Men in an Automobile." The item read as a wire dispatch, called the attack a "shooting affray," gave no motive, and offered no comment of the paper's own. It ran in a column of short items alongside a report that Bud Johnson had been taken from a sheriff and burned to death in Florida.

accounts.label: Memphis dispatch
accounts.gist: Two white men seated in an automobile opened fire on Black men coming out of a Beal street cafe, killing James Anderson and wounding three; the same men were supposed to have fired earlier on a carload of Black men on Fourth street.

framing.detail: The Ohio State Monitor ran the dispatch without comment under "MEMPHIS NEGRO KILLED," with the subhead naming the attackers as "Two White Men in an Automobile."
